job.title: Embedded Systems Design Engineer
job.description:
This is an exciting time to be joining a world leading wildlife tracking sales and engineering team. You will be based from Hawkes Bay New Zealand, whilst working closely with the Canadian based parent company.

The core essence of this highly specialized role is all about writing the code for the micro-controllers that make hardware come alive. And in this very clever business it is hardware that enables wildlife of all shapes and sizes to be tracked.  Our client specialises in manufacturing devices capable of tracking creatures spanning avian, freshwater, marine and terrestrial wildlife. This career opportunity places you at the heart of their technology offering.

This company’s Radio, Acoustic, Archival, GPS and Satellite instruments deployed on animals throughout the world provide insight to animal behaviour, how and where they spend their lives. We need an embedded systems design engineer to design, implement, and verify new products and feature, as well as to support existing product designs.

To be successful in this role you will need hands-on embedded systems design experience. You will be a good systems programmer and you’ll have solid knowledge of general circuit theory. Other key experience we are looking for includes:
  • Bachelor level qualification at the minimum, with hands-on software/firmware design experience,
  • Software exposure to the likes of C, C#, Java or similar,
  • Excellent familiarity with test & measurement equipment normally used in design work,
  • Good dexterity with miniature circuits and components;
  • Excellent communication skills (written and oral) and demonstrated ability of documenting the engineering work, very good command of English language is a must;
  • Practical knowledge of firmware design principles
  • Up-to-date familiarity with the latest electronic components, primary and secondary batteries, sensors and signal conditioning would be welcome assets as well.
  • Experience with programming techniques for ultra low-power battery operated systems would be a great asset although can be taught on the job.
This is a great role for a practically minded systems design engineer. If this sounds like you, then we really want to hear from you. Please apply through this seek portal or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Group Financial Controller
job.description:
An Internal promotion and clear growth trajectory with key global customers mean this finance leadership role provides an excellent career opportunity for a rising finance leader. This Gisborne-based Group Financial Controller role will be well suited to a commercially savvy, growth focused finance leader.

Corson is a family owned 100-year legacy business that has long been recognised for producing high-quality maize for food ingredients.

They were founded and continue to be grounded in Gisborne, but from there they reach far. They have real market strength, with operations in both NZ and Australia. Their close relationships with major FMCG customers see their finished product sitting as the base of many household food brands across Australasia.

Over the last 3 years the business has been in a recovery and reinvestment phase. They have invested in a new mill which is due to be commissioned later this year and implemented new accounting systems and process across the group focused on a digital future; so this is a great time to be joining the business.

As Group Financial Controller, you will provide the commercial and finance leadership to help steer them through their next phase of growth. You will lead the key aspects of financial management, reporting, compliance, cash flow management, risk and financial planning across the New Zealand and Australia operations. You will engage with operational leaders across the business to support business performance and profitability through providing meaningful financial insights and recommendations. This is a hands-on role, leading a small transactional finance and customer service team where you will oversee budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis for the group – ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting for the board and shareholders.

To be considered, you must be CA or CPA qualified with a strong knowledge of IFRS financial reporting standards, taxation and compliance. As well as proficiency in management accounting principles including pricing, revenue analysis and inventory cost analysis. Along with your strong technical expertise, you will need a big-picture mentality, be commercially astute and be comfortable challenging the status quo. An understanding of the complexities of manufacturing-based environments will be a real advantage here.
You may already be in a finance leadership role, or at the point in your career where a step up to a role like this is your next career challenge. There is a genuine pathway here for the right person.

Roles of this commercial nature are rare in Gisborne, you will be joining a great team with a huge commitment to growth and development. If you have the required finance expertise, people leadership experience and commercial strategic capacity to perform here, then please apply through this portal. Or call the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Manager - Strategic Investment & Regional Development
job.description:
Investment analysis, financial modelling expertise and a strong commercial mindset will see you right at home in this crucial Gisborne-based regional development role.

Trust Tairāwhiti is a regional development trust. Their strategic focus is to drive the economic development, community initiatives and investment strategies that support the wellbeing of people and place for Te Tairāwhiti.

Reporting to the GM of Economic Development, this role will spearhead the analysis, development and progression of strategic investment opportunities. Your oversight will help ensure alignment of capital, stakeholders, and delivery activity to achieve regional outcomes aligned with the Trust’s strategic plan. This is an influential position where you will be analysing and interrogating complex investment proposals, undertaking detailed financial analysis, and providing strategic advice to the Senior Leadship Team on opportunities, risks and trade-offs. You will collaborate with regional partners to progress infrastructure projects that will support an innovative, diverse, resilient and regenerative economy, while also contributing to the Trust’s mahi in Māori economic development.

Building and maintaining strong relationships will be a key part of your success. You’ll engage with the region’s commercial and economic influencers including iwi, business leaders, government agencies, Council and industry groups.

To be considered, you will need to be commercially astute, an expert in financial modelling and forecasting, and have the ability to analyse business cases and investment proposals with scrutiny. You may come from a banking, investment, consulting or financial analyst background and be ready for that next step up in your career. You will be known for your high capability in stakeholder engagement and relationship management, and have the ability to connect and network across the key touch points in Tairāwhiti. Relatability to the Tairāwhiti region and its economic landscape will be key in your success here.

Roles of this scope are rare in the Gisborne region. This is a chance to help shape the future prosperity of Te Tairāwhiti through strategic investment, regional development and meaningful collaboration with those who are driving change across the region.

If you have the relevant experience and are looking for a role where you can combine commercial expertise with genuine community impact, we'd love to hear from you.  Please apply through this portal or phone the team at Populous People on 06 875 8446 for a confidential discussion to learn more.

job.title: Workplace Safety Manager - Bel Group Central Hawke's Bay
job.description:
If you love being close to the action, connecting with people at every level, and playing an active role across the full spectrum of health safety and wellbeing initiatives, this senior leadership role offers the chance to get involved, make improvements, and see the results of your work every day.  Initiative, pragmatism and the ability and willingness to have courageous conversations will be crucial here.  

Bel Group is a privately owned dairy farming business with significant scale, managing extensive agricultural operations across multiple sites in Central Hawke's Bay.  Employing approximately 70 staff across nine farm units and more than 3,500 hectares of farmland in the Takapau area, the business has established a strong reputation for operational performance and long-term success.

This newly created role reports directly to the General Manager and offers the chance to take ownership of a critical business function while helping shape its future direction in workplace, health, safety and wellbeing.  This is not a role for someone who prefers to work from behind a desk.  This is a genuine partnership role, that will see you spending time on farm with operational teams to build credibility, identify critical risks, and provide practical, real-time health, safety and wellbeing advice and guidance.  Operating within a large-scale, high-risk and regulated environment, the scope is broad and varied and you can be guaranteed that no two days will be the same.  
  
Your core mandate will be to ensure legislative requirements and industry best practice standards are met, support robust risk and incident management processes, develop and build training and capability programmes, and drive continuous improvement across all areas of health, safety, and wellbeing.  You will bring a hearty combination of energy, maturity and resilience to challenge existing practices, drive positive behavioural change, and embed a culture where safety, wellbeing, and accountability are part of everyday decision-making.  
  
We are looking for a hands-on health and safety leader who thrives in complex operational environments and has the credibility to influence at every level of the business.  You must hold relevant health and safety qualifications, have working knowledge of NZ health and safety regulations and legislation, and ideally have gained experience from within a farming, agricultural or horticultural environment.  You may be in a current health, safety and wellbeing leadership role now and looking for a fresh change, or you could be on your way to the next step in your career.  Either way, it will be important that you are able to hit the ground running on-site in Central Hawke’s Bay.  For the right person, this a rare chance to leave a lasting mark on a growing organisation, shape the future of workplace safety, and make a genuine difference to the lives of those who work within it.  Remuneration will reflect your experience. Please apply directly through this portal, or for further information, call the team at Populous People for a confidential discussion on 068758446.

job.title: Chief Engineer
job.description:
This newly created civil engineering leadership role will help shape the next phase of growth and optimisation for a highly regarded multidisciplinary civil construction and infrastructure company. You will lead and develop multi-site engineering and project delivery teams, strengthen risk and assurance practices, and position the Group’s technical capability for continued success as it expands into new markets.

Lattey Group is a multidisciplinary construction and engineering company with 75 years of market experience and 100 plus people across their Hastings and Levin sites. Its reputation for innovative, safe and efficient infrastructure solutions is built across five key divisions, including civil engineering, precast concrete manufacturing, crane hire, and the highly effective HEX-LOC® system.

As Chief Engineer, you will be Lattey Group’s senior engineering authority; providing engineering leadership across bridge, structural, piling, marine, foundation, precast and infrastructure construction projects delivered throughout New Zealand.

Your responsibilities will span engineering and people leadership, governance, technical assurance, and frontline civil engineering decisions across the Group’s physical works, construction methodologies and project delivery. You’ll provide independent oversight and direction across project planning, site assessment, option development, design and sign-off, constructability, construction methodology, technical risk, compliance, and delivery, including across engineered lift plans, critical lifts, crane-related engineering activities and associated construction risks.

You will also oversee site assessments and design solutions to optimise the use of their highly regarded HEX-LOC® system. This includes assessing technical suitability, defining system configurations and design boundaries, and developing robust solutions that deliver durable, resilient, sustainable, whole-of-life value for clients.

This will suit a Chartered Professional Engineer, or an experienced senior engineering leader with the ability to achieve or maintain chartered status. You must be equally confident leading people, setting engineering standards, and providing timely technical direction to frontline teams. You will combine sound judgement in managing engineering risk and opportunity with a natural, engaging leadership style. A capable team is already in place; your focus will be to build its capability further, and to represent the Group as a trusted technical authority with clients, designers, regulators, asset owners, and the wider engineering profession.

If you have the engineering expertise, an engaging approach to team leadership, and ambition to lead in a substantial civil and infrastructure business, we welcome your interest. Lattey Group has big growth plans, with the innovation, capability, and experience to expand well beyond the region. Remuneration and reward reflect the scope and seniority of this role. Please apply through this portal or, for a confidential discussion, contact Rachel Cornwall at Populous People on 0272 565 620.

job.title: Factory Production Foreman
job.description:
This is a great opportunity to join a modern manufacturing business that is focused on innovation and delivering world-class products to customers throughout New Zealand and international markets.
  
If you are a motivated production leader who thrives in a hands-on environment and enjoys developing people while driving operational excellence, we'd love to hear from you. Relatability to fabrication and engineering environments will be highly regarded.
  
Our client, is a leading New Zealand-based manufacturer with a strong reputation for designing and producing innovative agricultural equipment supplied throughout New Zealand and international markets. We are looking for a hands-on production leader who can drive productivity, quality workmanship, continuous improvement, and team performance.
  
This key leadership role is responsible for leading and coordinating all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient and profitable production of assembled machines. You will be accountable for production planning, quality control, health and safety compliance, continuous improvement, assisting with research and development projects and inventory management while fostering a positive and high performance culture.
  
Your responsibilities will span day-to-day production, ensuring standard operating procedures (SOPs), quality and safety protocols are maintained to ensure top quality products are produced for their customers. You will ensure effective resource allocation and planning, continued efficiency gains, along with development and growth for your staff.
  
To be considered, you must have previous leadership experience within a manufacturing, engineering, fabrication, or industrial production environment. Either way, you must be a natural people leader who enjoys being across the floor each and every day; driving efficiency, problem solving, and ensuring optimisation across all aspects of the site. You must have a continuous improvement mindset and preferably have experience implementing Lean Manufacturing.
  
If you have the expertise and people skills required, and you are ready to take the next step in your manufacturing career, then we would love to hear from you. Your experience will be well rewarded. Please apply directly through this portal and be sure to include a resume and cover letter. For more information on this role, call the Populous People team for a confidential discussion on 06 875 8446.

job.title: Finance & Accounts Specialist - Driving Miss Daisy
job.description:
We love building this team; this is a great opportunity to join a commercially successful, community-facing, New Zealand wide business. If you are experienced in accounts processing and are known for your attention to detail and forensic ability to pick up anomalies, then this could be a great role to consider.  

Driving Miss Daisy is recognised as the nationwide market leader in the companion driving sector - they are loved by many for their service and support across the country. Their highly effective franchise model operates in 85 different franchise territories from Invercargill to Kerikeri, with their head office based here in Havelock North. They have recently secured a significant contract with ACC and they want to expand their team to ensure they continue to meet their goal of administrative excellence. Their continued aspirations for the development and growth of their franchisees means that they rely increasingly on accurate data and quality analysis to help drive commercial performance for every franchise owner across the country. 

Working closely with the Senior Data Analyst and reporting to the General Manager, your focus will be on the administration that sits around ACC invoicing across each of the franchises. This will include remittance reconciliation, processing franchisee-specific payment batches, franchisee compliance and reporting, as well as supporting with general accounts administration.

There is an exciting new system integration here, and ample scope to make this role your own. Competency with Excel and Xero will be crucial, and you must have the ability to read beyond the numbers and uncover anomalies and errors across sets of data. This role will see you engaging directly with ACC to query and resolve any issues. Importantly, you will bring a well-developed, inquisitive communication style, where you are not afraid to question how things are done.

If you have the required expertise and are keen to join a business that makes a significant difference empowering the lives of kiwis every day, then we would love to hear from you. Please apply directly through this portal, or for further information, call the team at Populous People for a confidential chat on 06 875 8446.

job.title: Sales Director - Nibblish
job.description:
If you are an expert in leading and expanding FMCG sales channels and categories this could be a great sales leadership opportunity. You will be driving both the New Zealand and Australian sales strategy for Nibblish, and you get to do it from the home base of Hawkes Bay. Career and great living all in one.
  
Nibblish is a fast-growing ANZ snacking brand, with its head office in the heart of Havelock North. Join a great team and an exciting brand; delivering innovative fruit products into more than 2,000 mainstream supermarkets across New Zealand and Australia. The business is achieving strong double-digit growth, led by Australia, where its presence with Coles and Woolworths continues to expand. Your role is to protect, expand and grow its shelf presence even further.
  
As Sales Director, reporting directly to the CEO and founder, you will own and evolve the ANZ commercial delivery for Nibblish. Your role will be to build on the strong growth already established with Coles, Woolworths AU, Foodstuffs NZ and Woolworths NZ. And you will have genuine scope to define the next horizon of sales growth and execution across Australia and New Zealand. 
  
Sales and relationship management, and commercial leadership intersect here. You will be responsible for delivering the ANZ sales and operating margin budgets, and will work closely with the CFO to support profitability analysis. You will be someone who can actively bring forward profitable growth initiatives; identifying new customers, new channels, optimising promotional plans, and adjacent category opportunities will sit with you.
  
This role sits across the end-to-end commercial relationship with every major existing retailer Nibblish trades with in Australia and New Zealand. Familiarity and experience in dealing with Coles and Woolworths AU will be highly regarded.  And strong account and category management relationships in Foodstuffs NZ and Woolworths NZ will be essential. You will represent Nibblish directly with these retailers, negotiating trade terms, establishing joint business plans, and ensuring optimised portfolio ranging. And you will also work closely with distributor partners, as well as build direct relationships with key independent and specialty retailers.
  
This is suited to an experienced FMCG sales leader and senior account manager. If you are not already at sales director level, this move will feel like your next natural step. Either way you will know that channel presence and shelf space is everything in FMCG. You must have the category management expertise and the resilience to build strong relationships with key decision makers and influencers in store and in market across New Zealand and Australia.
  
Join a great crew, passionate about their work. You will be well rewarded and supported by business owners determined to ensure balance and enjoyment in your day. If you have the FMCG sales leadership expertise, and you relate well to the pace and innovation of SMEs on a growth trajectory then please apply through this portal or telephone Rachel Cornwall at Populous People on 0272 565620 to learn more.
